extracted.intended_audience: general readers, students, and researchers interested in labor disputes and the entertainment industry
extracted.subtask_description: Extraction of the substantive strategies, procedural choices, and evaluative considerations described in the encyclopedia article about the 2007–08 Writers Guild of America strike. Focuses on tactics, negotiation approaches, public outreach, solidarity considerations, and measures of impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Picketing tactics and scheduling
rubrics_metrics.description: For its second week of picketing, the WGA reduced their studio strike list from fourteen to ten, shifted picketing hours to earlier in the day, and scheduled a series of daily strike themes ranging from "Bring-A-Star-To-Picket-With-You" (also called "Cast Day") to "Bring-Your-Kids" special events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples given as guidance: reduce and prioritize targets, move hours to increase visibility/impact, use themed days (e.g., Cast Day, family days) to increase participation and media attention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct public outreach and online PR
rubrics_metrics.description: The WGA made a direct appeal to the public to explain the issues behind the strike, including use of online videos and blogs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use digital channels (videos, blogs) to explain grievances to the public, shape narrative, and build public support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Symbolic/creative protest actions
rubrics_metrics.description: WGA strike captains encouraged fans to mail pencils to the film and TV moguls en masse. They also considered unorthodox methods, including performing a mock exorcism against Warner Bros. and holding the last rites for the former MBA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Symbolic acts (mass mailings, theatrical stunts) can generate publicity and solidarity; the page lists these as tactics used or considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal to other unions and cross-union solidarity
rubrics_metrics.description: The WGA appealed to members of crew and industry craft unions, including the Teamsters and IATSE, some of whom may not have been aware that their union also received residuals to pay for health and pension programs, and that they were expected to directly benefit from residual gains made by the WGA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inform other unions of how proposed gains affect them (e.g., residuals funding benefits) and solicit their support; outreach to allied unions is a deliberate strategy to broaden pressure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divide-and-conquer negotiation strategy (interim deals)
rubrics_metrics.description: In late December, the WGA announced a new "divide and conquer" strategy designed to break the solidarity of the AMPTP by negotiating strategic interim deals with individual networks, studios, and production companies who were willing to agree to the WGA's proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tactic: secure interim agreements with willing companies to create pressure on remaining companies. Examples: deals with Worldwide Pants, United Artists, The Weinstein Company, Media Rights Capital, Spyglass Entertainment, Marvel Studios. Noted risk: resentment among members if some writers work while others remain on strike.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver policy for awards telecasts and targeted pressure
rubrics_metrics.description: The WGA announced it would (and would not) issue waivers for awards ceremonies — issuing waivers for some events (e.g., SAG Awards, Film Independent's Spirit Awards, NAACP Image Awards, the Grammys) while denying waivers for the Golden Globes and Academy Awards; denied waivers led to celebrity boycotts and forced format/tactical changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use waivers selectively as a lever: grant waivers when an organization demonstrates 'honesty' and 'respectful treatment' or reaches acceptable terms; deny waivers to apply pressure by undermining the event's viability and pressuring producers/hosts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balancing solidarity with contractual/legal constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: The Screen Actors Guild and AFTRA contracts with the AMPTP both contain a "no strike" clause, meaning working members of the acting unions are not supposed to walk off their set in support of another union's strike. However, many actors, backed by their unions, expressed their support and solidarity with the writers' strike, some marching and refusing to cross WGA picket lines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider contractual obligations (no-strike clauses, AFTRA TV Code) when soliciting ally action; navigate legal limits while encouraging solidarity where possible (e.g., public statements, PSAs, selective participation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Managing targets and internal decisions about who to picket
rubrics_metrics.description: The guild stated it had no plans to target Leno and O'Brien with protests such as were aimed at non-WGA member Carson Daly, because some shows had independent agreements (e.g., David Letterman's Worldwide Pants interim agreement allowed returns with writers). WGA assured HFPA it would not picket the Golden Globes after HFPA's 'honesty and its honorable and respectful treatment of the guild.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decide picket targets based on contractual status and interim agreements; avoid picketing organizations that have reached acceptable interim terms or shown cooperative behavior to preserve moral authority and strategic alliances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leveraging celebrity and fan involvement
rubrics_metrics.description: Numerous actors, comedians, and other celebrities marched with writers, participated in PSAs, or otherwise expressed support; organized fan groups (e.g., Fans4Writers, Xena fans) walked picket lines and provided food drops.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recruit visible public figures and organized fan bases to increase visibility, sustain picket lines, and demonstrate broad support; use celebrity participation in rallies and PSAs as PR leverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measuring economic and audience impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimates and studies were used to quantify the strike's effects: Milken Institute estimated $2.1 billion in economic losses and net loss of 37,700 jobs; AMPTP estimated WGA writers and IATSE crewmembers lost $342.8 million in wages; Nielsen reported a 6.8% decline in average primetime ratings for the strike months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track and publicize quantifiable metrics (economic losses, job losses, wages lost, ratings/viewership declines) to demonstrate impact and influence public/political opinion; cite reputable studies and polls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media/content strategy for shows returning without writers
rubrics_metrics.description: Some talk shows returned to air without writers citing non-writing staff layoffs as a reason (e.g., Jay Leno, Conan O'Brien), and some programs were rebranded to show respect (e.g., The Daily Show renamed 'A Daily Show with Jon Stewart'). The WGA accused networks of forcing hosts back on air by threatening jobs and said it would picket them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anticipate and respond to employer tactics (shows returning without writers) by naming/rebranding, publicizing staff-impact rationales, and using pickets/PR to contest perceived strike-breaking actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pattern bargaining and downstream union effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Any increase for benefits or residual gains made by the WGA are likely to be demanded by other entertainment industry labor unions when their contracts expire — a practice known as pattern bargaining — so WGA outcomes set templates (e.g., SAG and DGA contracts expiring in 2008).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that a lead union's agreement sets expectations for related unions; use outcomes strategically to influence broader industry bargaining but also anticipate ripple effects (other unions may follow or react).

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal solidarity and member morale management
rubrics_metrics.description: The divide-and-conquer interim-deal approach contained risk for the WGA, however, as there was a risk that some members may resent a few writers working while others were still on strike.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weigh short-term tactical gains against long-term internal cohesion; communicate openly with members about interim deals and mitigation measures to minimize resentment and maintain solidarity.
